entries.title: AI voice cloning calls
entries.summary: A caller uses a short AI-cloned audio sample of a family member's voice, often built from a few seconds of social media video, to fake an emergency and pressure you into sending money fast.
red_flags: Urgent request for money from a 'relative' who sounds slightly off or won't video call
Caller insists you keep it secret from other family members
Pressure to pay immediately via gift cards, crypto, or wire transfer
prevention_tips: Hang up and call the person back on a number you already have saved
Agree on a family verification phrase nobody else would know
Never send money based on a call alone, verify through a second channel

entries.title: Deepfake video scams
entries.summary: Fabricated video of a public figure, executive, or official is used to promote a fake investment, fake news story, or fraudulent authorization on a video call.
red_flags: Unnatural blinking, lighting, or lip-sync in the video
The video pushes you toward an urgent financial decision
It appears only on an unofficial account or unfamiliar link
prevention_tips: Check whether the same claim appears on the person's or company's verified official channels
Search for the video or claim alongside the word 'scam' or 'fake'
Treat any investment 'endorsement' from a video with real skepticism

entries.title: Fake toll & government texts
entries.summary: Government and bank impersonation remains the most reported scam category. A common current version is a text claiming you owe an unpaid toll or fee, threatening late charges or registration suspension.
red_flags: Text about an unpaid toll, fine, or fee with a link to 'pay now'
Claims to be from police, tax authorities, or a benefits agency
Creates urgency with threats of legal action or account suspension
prevention_tips: Go directly to the agency's official site or app instead of clicking the link
Real government agencies rarely demand instant payment by text
Report suspicious texts to your carrier or local consumer protection agency

entries.title: Romance scams
entries.summary: An online relationship, often built over weeks on a dating app or social media, is used to eventually ask for money for an emergency, travel costs, or a shared investment opportunity.
red_flags: Professes strong feelings quickly, avoids video calls or meeting in person
Has a story involving travel, military deployment, or overseas work
Eventually introduces a financial emergency or investment 'opportunity'
prevention_tips: Reverse-image-search their profile photo
Never send money or gift cards to someone you haven't met in person
Talk to a friend or family member before sending money to an online contact

entries.title: Investment & crypto scams
entries.summary: Promises of guaranteed high returns, often tied to crypto, AI-themed funds, or real estate, pressure victims to invest quickly. This category causes the largest reported financial losses of any scam type.
red_flags: Guaranteed or unusually high returns with 'low risk'
Pressure to act immediately before a limited window closes
Unregistered platforms or advisors you can't independently verify
prevention_tips: Verify any advisor or platform through an official financial regulator
Be skeptical of any 'guaranteed return' claim, legitimate investing carries risk
Slow down, real opportunities don't disappear if you take a day to check

entries.title: Gift card & instant payment pressure
entries.summary: Regardless of the story, scammers converge on the same demand: pay through gift cards, cryptocurrency, wire transfer, or a peer-to-peer app, since these are hard to trace or reverse.
red_flags: Insists gift cards or crypto are the only accepted payment
Asks you to read out gift card codes over the phone
Claims a mistaken payment on a peer-to-peer app and asks you to send it back
prevention_tips: No legitimate agency or business asks to be paid in gift cards
Confirm any 'mistaken payment' claim directly with your bank first
Pause before any payment method feels unusually specific or urgent

entries.title: Fake job offers
entries.summary: A job offer, often unsolicited over text or social media, requires little effort, promises high pay, and eventually asks for personal information, a fee, or check-cashing that leaves the victim liable.
red_flags: You're hired without an interview or with a very short one
Asked to pay for training, equipment, or a background check upfront
Involves depositing a check and forwarding part of the funds elsewhere
prevention_tips: Research the company independently, don't rely only on the recruiter's links
Legitimate employers never ask you to pay them to get hired
Never deposit and forward funds from an unfamiliar check

entries.title: Social media shopping scams
entries.summary: Ads on social platforms offer expensive items at steep discounts. Shopping scams are now the most commonly reported scam type originating on social media.
red_flags: Prices far below market rate with a countdown timer
Store has no reviews, or only recently created social accounts
Checkout redirects to an unfamiliar payment page
prevention_tips: Search the store name alongside 'reviews' or 'scam' before buying
Use a credit card, not a direct bank transfer, for purchase protection
Be wary of ads that only appear on social feeds with no real storefront
